_note: Public template. Copy to axon-overlay/config/comms.json and fill real values there — never here. comms resolves config from $SJEL_COMMS_CONFIG > $SJEL_PERSONAL_ROOT/config/comms.json > capabilities/comms/comms.config.json at runtime (see src/config.rs Config::load). Every field is optional; the tool runs zero-config against the shared local store with only the built-in classification heuristics. There is no database key: PRD Q45 made the store path a deployment fact ($SJEL_DB_PATH, else $SJEL_PERSONAL_ROOT/data/axon/axon.db).
_comment_google_env: Path to the KEY=value env file holding GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN (mint the refresh token once via auth/get-refresh-token.ts). Defaults to $SJEL_PERSONAL_ROOT/config/comms.env. Sweeps are read-only; authenticated, confirmed dashboard actions may archive a stored thread or move it to Gmail Trash.
_comment_api_secret: Shared secret for every route except /health and /ready — reads included since comms moved onto the inbound gate in libs/sjel-server. Path to a file containing the bearer token (or JSON with auth.api_key), never the token itself. Without it those routes answer 403 rather than opening. Generate a private file with: openssl rand -hex -out path/to/file 32 && chmod 600 path/to/file. This value wins over the deployment-wide SJEL_INBOUND_TOKEN_FILE (schemas/deployment.env.example); point both at one file to converge on a single token. The local dashboard's Vite proxy reads this same reference at startup and injects it server-side; browser JavaScript never receives the value. Restart Comms and the dashboard after rotating it. The browser extension and direct CLI calls also use this value.
_comment_enrichment_drain_minutes: How often comms-server drains the summary backlog, in minutes (default 15). Ingest-triggered enrichment only reaches items that arrive while the inference server is up; without this pass, items ingested during an outage stay empty until someone runs `comms summarize --pending` by hand. The retry ledger bounds it: three failed attempts with exponential backoff, each failure recording its error class. Set 0 to disable when something else owns the schedule.
_comment_digest_drain_minutes: How often comms-server retries feed digests that failed retryably, in minutes (default 15). Separate from enrichment_drain_minutes because the two write different things — that one fills feed_items.summary, this one fills content_digests. It runs offset half a period from the enrichment drain rather than alongside it: both prefill the same transcripts on the same local backend, so firing together is the one schedule guaranteed to make them contend. Set 0 to leave digests manual-press-only.
_comment_capacity_alert_after: How many consecutive capacity aborts from the local inference server before the automatic passes raise it instead of absorbing it (default 3). One abort is another prefill in flight and self-heals; three in a row means waiting will not write the row. The alert is a line on the server's stderr plus `summarizer.capacity` on GET /feed/evaluation/status, which carries the streak for anyone who was not watching at the time. Set 0 to disable.
_comment_gmail_maintenance_minutes: How often comms-server retries durable Gmail actions and reconciles up to 200 stored thread locations from metadata labels (default 15 minutes). It reads labels only, never bodies or attachments. Set 0 to disable automatic maintenance; the authenticated manual reconciliation route remains available.
_comment_inbox_sweep_minutes: How often comms-server pulls new inbox proposals, in minutes. 0 (the shipped default) disables it: an unattended job that reads a mailbox is opt-in per machine, never something a fresh clone starts doing. The manual preview stays available either way — `comms sweep --dry-run` prints proposals without storing any, and the board's own sweep button is unaffected.
_comment_inbox_sweep_max_threads: Newest-N threads per scheduled pass (default 25, clamped 1-100). A bound rather than a cursor on purpose: a cursor advancing every run would walk backwards through the entire mailbox over days, which is the unbounded rescan this schedule avoids. Re-reading the newest page costs nothing because proposals upsert on Gmail thread id and preserve human decisions. Paging deeper stays a manual, cursor-carrying call.
_comment_inbox_sweep_quiet_hours: Local hours [start, end) in which the schedule holds off, as "22-7". Omit for no quiet window. Wraps midnight. Only the unattended schedule respects it; manual sweeps do not, because the point is to stop background traffic, not to lock you out of your own tool. An unparseable value means no window rather than an all-day one — a schedule that silently never runs looks identical to a broken connector.
_comment_ingest_allowed_origins: Exact scheme://host:port origins that POST /ingest may fetch even though they resolve to an address inside this machine or this network. Empty by default, and empty is the right value on a real machine: the destination guard in src/media.rs (check_destination) exists because every Axon service binds 127.0.0.1, so an ingested link would otherwise drive an internal API. An entry clears one origin, never a host — listing http://127.0.0.1:8099 does not clear http://127.0.0.1:8086. Matching is on the URL as written, so a public name that resolves to loopback still does not match. tools/demo-up is the only user of this field in the repository: the demo seeds Comms from a synthetic loopback origin, and demo/README.md records why.
_comment_quality_flags: Computed review-queue thresholds. Passing extraction fixtures retain 39.7–89.6% of total raw text, preserve 100% judged useful text, and leak 0% judged boilerplate; the defaults round that observed total-retention envelope outward to 39–90% and keep leakage at 0%. summary_attempt_warning=2 flags the attempt before the existing three-attempt cap parks an item. Flagging never calls a provider or enriches an item.
_comment_keeper_export_dir: Optional directory. When set, `comms keep <id>` also writes a distilled markdown note (title, url, date, summary — never the raw transcript). Leave unset to disable export.
_comment_obsidian: Optional Obsidian vault the feed library projects into (PRD Q49). Same block shape as trips.json. When set, every saved item (status 'keeper') becomes one note in Resources/Sources/ and unsaving removes it; `comms export-sources` reconciles the folder with the server down. Absent leaves the bridge off — no vault, no writes. This is a write destination bounded to one folder, unlike vault_link_sources below, which refuses a root because it reads.
_comment_inference: Comms asks the shared inference.json for the 'summarization', 'embedding' and 'reranking' roles. Backend URLs, model ids, prefixes and key-file references belong in <overlay>/config/inference.json, never here. A missing reranker preserves semantic scores; a missing embedding role degrades to explicitly labelled lexical relevance.
_comment_relevance: General Feed personalization. profile_paths accepts exact Markdown files or non-recursive directories of focus lenses. Embedding selects lens candidates; reranking scores those query-document pairs.
_comment_travel_context: Optional read-only Trips context for Feed ranking. Comms reads the existing Trips HTTP API, retains only a bounded snapshot of upcoming plan title, destinations, dates and interests, and keeps using the last successful snapshot during a temporary outage. Traveler names and itinerary payloads are not copied.
_comment_finance_context: Finance owns mail-derived transaction candidates. Comms sends only normalized fields over this loopback contract; source-account choices come from Finance's configured import profiles.
_comment_vault_link_sources: Explicit Markdown files that may supply Feed links. Never point this at the vault root. heading limits a messy note such as Scratchpad.md to one deliberate section and stops at the next heading of the same or higher level. A missing heading returns zero candidates. Fenced code, frontmatter and credential-looking URLs are ignored.
_comment_feed_sources: General Feed collectors. Omit this field to use the public GitHub Trending daily and recent arXiv AI defaults; set [] to disable all. arxiv.query uses the official arXiv search_query grammar. limit is bounded by each adapter. Personal saved queries belong only in axon-overlay.
_comment_feed_sources_data_class: data_class is REQUIRED on every source and has no default: c0 (Public), c1 (Mine), c2 (Others) or c3 (Secret). It is the declaration every item this collector stores is classified with, and the only way an item becomes c0 at all. A source you are not sure about is c1 — an item nobody declared stays c1 and never reaches a cloud provider verbatim, which is the intended answer, not a gap.
_comment_rules: Config-driven classification rules, evaluated first (first match wins) before the built-in heuristics. Each rule: { match: { from_contains?: [..], subject_contains?: [..], has_list_unsubscribe?: bool }, stream: one of aktiv|issue|feed|werbung|belege|steuern|sonstiges, note: '<one-line rationale>' }. Keep anything personal (real sender addresses) in the private overlay, never here.
